problem:
The equation

$$
p{x}^{2}+qx-6={x}^{2}+7x-6
$$

is true for all values of $x,$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. What is the value of $pq?$

$pq=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Since the equation is true for all values of $x,$ the expressions on both sides must be exactly the same. That means the coefficients of the matching powers of $x$ must be equal.

Let's compare the coefficients:

- The coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ on the left-hand side is $p,$ and on the right-hand side it is $1.$ So, we have 

$$
p=1.
$$

- The coefficient of $x$ on the left-hand side is $q,$ and on the right-hand side it is $7.$ So, we have 

$$
q=7.
$$

Now, we compute the product:

$$
\begin{aligned}pq & =1\cdot 7 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$
